one_month_reasoning: No Oracle earnings in the window (Q2 FY27 is due mid-December). The scheduled events are industry read-throughs: Q3 results from Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta (~Oct 28-29) and Amazon (Oct 29) will bring the first numeric 2027 capex guides. The standing capex view expects these to be at or above the ~$0.93-1.03T Big-4 consensus. A strong guide helps the AI-infrastructure trade but also restokes the debt/financing worries that have driven ORCL's credit spreads. NVIDIA reports just after the window. Project-finance headlines (New Mexico force majeure, bank loans trading below par) and OpenAI funding news are the main idiosyncratic risk. Given these offsetting effects, the forecast is centred on spot ($143.41, P(>=spot) ~0.505) with a monthly sigma of ~16% (56%/3.5), and no directional call.

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E (CY2028E EPS $12.1 x 15x = $182; Oct-2027 investors price CY28) and EV/EBITDA (NTM-at-Oct-27 EBITDA ~$65B x 10x less ~$160B net debt over ~3.1B shares = $158), 50/50 -> ~$170. Multiples sit below the peer median (21.3x CY27 P/E, ~14.5x EV/EBITDA) for BBB- leverage, negative FCF and ~50% OpenAI RPO concentration.

Peer forward EV/EBITDA median ~14.5x (derived from TTM ratios less ~1y EBITDA growth; range ~5.8x CRWV to ~33x NOW). Oracle's capex intensity (FY27 capex $90-95B gross vs ~$40B EBITDA) makes EBITDA overstate owner earnings, so it is placed between CRWV (5.8x) and the mega-cap median.
Debt $169.1B less cash $37.1B = $132B today; FY27 net cash capex <= $70B against OCF incl. prepayments (Q1 OCF $23.1B), S&P sees FOCF -$42B in FY27; partly funded by $20B ATM equity -> ~+$28B net.
Q1 FY27 diluted 3.00B; market cap $434.6B / $143.35 = 3.03B; + ~2-3% further issuance.

bear.story: OpenAI (about half of RPO, $60B/yr from 2027) renegotiates, slows or delays Stargate take-up as its own funding gap (FT: -$278B cumulative FCF 2026-30) bites; site delays like Project Jupiter (force majeure, $18B loan <90c) spread; S&P/Moody's cut to junk; FY28 EPS cut to ~$8.5-9 and the market pays ~10x.

base.story: OCI keeps converting backlog (RPO $664B, ~half within 36 months; GPU utilisation ~98%, renewal pricing +20%), FY27 guide ($90B rev, $8.10 EPS) is met, FY28 guide in June 2027 roughly matches consensus; credit stays BBB-; multiple stays depressed at ~13-14x CY28 EPS ~ $12.

bull.story: OpenAI's revenue ramp (~$70B annualised) and funding remove counterparty fear, hyperscaler 2027 capex guides (Big-4 base $1.08T) confirm demand, prepay/BYO-hardware model caps net capex and FCF turns toward breakeven in FY28; CDS tightens and the stock re-rates to ~19-20x CY28 EPS of ~$12.5.

comps_summary.peer_range: CY2027 P/E 8.5x (ADBE) to 27.0x (NOW), n=10 (CRWV loss-making, excluded); forward EV/EBITDA ~5.8x (CRWV) to ~33x (NOW), n=11. All P/Es on one basis: calendar-2027 consensus EPS (Yahoo), with fiscal years calendarised (MSFT 1/2 FY27 + 1/2 FY28; CRM/WDAY FY ending Jan-2028; ADBE FY Nov-2027; SAP derived from StockAnalysis fwd P/E / 1.15). Peer EV/EBITDA forward values are our derivations from StockAnalysis TTM ratios, adjusted for ~1 year of EBITDA growth, so they are approximate.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: ORCL trades at 14.6x CY27 consensus EPS ($9.81) and ~11x CY27 EBITDA, about 30% below the peer median. We apply 15x CY28 EPS and 10x NTM EBITDA: inside the peer range, near the bottom quartile (IBM/CRM/WDAY on P/E; between CRWV and the mega-caps on EV/EBITDA).
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The discount should persist through the horizon for four reasons. (1) Balance sheet: S&P BBB- (Jul-2026), both S&P and Moody's on negative outlook, 5y CDS a record ~203-227bp vs NVDA ~79bp. Every mega-cap peer is A or better with net cash or low leverage. (2) Cash generation: FCF is negative (TTM -$28.7B, Q1 -$5.4B) and S&P sees FY27 FOCF of -$42B, while peers fund capex from operating cash. (3) Concentration: ~half of the $664B RPO is from OpenAI, a loss-making counterparty. (4) Earnings quality: the mix is shifting to lower-margin GPU IaaS (gross margin falling during the ramp), and there is ongoing dilution ($20B ATM, mandatory convertible). We do not apply a full CRWV-style discount: Oracle has ~$40B+ EBITDA from database, apps and support, which no neocloud has.

thesis_break_reason: A sustained move below ~$105 (about 8% under the 52-week low of $114.50, -27%) would most likely mean a fundamental break rather than volatility: OpenAI renegotiating or deferring its ~$60B/yr commitment, a downgrade to high yield that shuts the project-finance market (Project Jupiter's $18B loan is already below 90c), or an FY28 guide that implies EPS well below ~$10. At that point the stock would be pricing about 10x CY27 consensus, which only makes sense if the backlog is impaired.

reasoning: Price $143.41, down 51% in a year and 56% from the peak, with 56% realised vol. Primary data: Q1 FY27 (Sep 10) revenue $19.3B +30%, OCI $7.4B +121%, non-GAAP EPS $1.92 (beat), RPO $664B, OCF $23.1B, capex $28.5B gross/$18.0B net of prepayments, FCF -$5.4B. FY27 guide is >=$90B revenue and $8.10 EPS; capex $90-95B gross, <= $70B net. $20B ATM equity was completed in Q1. Industry/chain evidence: (a) Demand looks real. Industry-wide GPU utilisation and renewal pricing are firm (Oracle ~98% utilisation, +20% renewals; the Silicon Data H100 index ticked up w/w). The capex standing view has Big-4 2027 at $1.08T base and Oracle CY27 gross capex at ~$110B. (b) The main customer's ability to pay improved: OpenAI went from missing targets in early 2026 (WSJ) to ~$70B annualised by September (Sacra), but its commitments of >$1.4T dwarf that. (c) The financing chain is the weak link. S&P cut to BBB- citing OpenAI concentration. CDS are at records. Banks retreated on Michigan (PIMCO had to anchor). The Project Jupiter $18B loan trades <90c after a force-majeure notice. Valuation: consensus CY27 EPS $9.81 gives 14.6x vs a peer median of 21.3x on a consistent calendar-2027 basis. I keep the discount (leverage, negative FCF, concentration) and value at 15x CY28 EPS of ~$12.1 plus 10x NTM EBITDA net of ~$160B debt. The blended FV is ~$170 (sell-side average PT $238 is not used as an anchor). Scenarios 27% bear $88 / 50% base $158 / 23% bull $245 give a mean of ~$159. The ladder is a lognormal mixture (sigmas 0.38/0.24/0.24), and the left tail was fattened slightly so the overall spread matches the stock's ~56% vol. Result: P(>=spot) ~0.58 and median ~$155. The skew is modestly positive, because the valuation is cheap relative to the chain, but the 27% bear weight reflects real counterparty and financing risk. Research was limited by Twelve Data/Alpha Vantage plan limits; peer estimates are from Yahoo consensus pages and EV/EBITDA forwards are our derivations.
